title: ZenithBank - Vendor Risk Questionnaire Walkthrough
summary: Walkthrough of ZenithBank vendor risk questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ-style). Discussed SOC 2 scope, ISO 27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, data residency, and evidence packaging. Agreed next steps: deliver SIG export + control mapping, share SOC 2 Type II report & ISO cert, provide demo of audit log export, and schedule technical follow-up for KMS integration details.
next_steps: Jordan: Send SIG/CAIQ export and control mapping spreadsheet by 2025-02-18
Priya Nair: Share short demo of audit log export and retention UI next week
Liam Chen: Draft KMS integration runbook and options for BYOK vs Redwood-managed KMS
Alex (Zenith): Circulate internal VRR and mark any control gaps by 2025-02-25
Schedule deep-dive on network segmentation and VPC peering (SE-led)
action_items: Jordan Miles: Deliver SIG/CAIQ PDF + CSV control export (due 2025-02-18)
Priya Nair: Record 10-min screen capture showing audit log export and retention settings (due 2025-02-20)
Liam Chen: Provide KMS architecture options (Redwood KMS, customer BYOK via KMS/HSM) with pros/cons (due 2025-02-21)
Alex Romero: Provide list of mandatory evidence items from Zenith security team (due 2025-02-25)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-14 15:00 UTC | Duration 55m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Solutions), Alex Romero (Zenith CISO), Priya Patel (Zenith SecPM), Martin Osei (Zenith Procurement), Sandeep Rao (Zenith Cloud Ops)
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time, we'll go through the vendor risk questionnaire you sent over and map to Redwood controls. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE, Priya is our security engineer, Liam does KMS and infra.
[00:12] Alex: Thanks, Jordan. We got a big VRR, mostly SIG-alike. We want to understand scope — hosted versus dedicated versus private. Also need SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO certs.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Hi all — quick note, we'll call out where Redwood has standard artifacts and where we need specific evidence, like system configs or screenshots. Some auto-questions on the VRQ sometimes expect a "yes" with evidence link.
[00:40] Martin: Also procurement wants to know the timeline for evidence — we have a quarterly vendor review window.
[00:48] Jordan: Understood — we'll try to align. Quick agenda: SIG mapping, SOC2/ISO documents, SSO/RBAC model, audit logs/retention, encryption/KMS, data residency, then next steps. Sound OK?
[00:58] Alex: Yep.
[01:05] Priya Patel: One clarification: we asked about multi-tenant data separation. Can you confirm how isolation works on hosted?
[01:12] Priya Nair: Sure — hosted is multi-tenant; we logically isolate at application and tenancy layers, prefix KV cache separation, per-customer model routing and encryption keys. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. (audio: slight overlap)
[01:28] Sandeep: For Dedicated, is there physical host affinity or just reserved GPU pools? We need to map that to our segmentation controls.
[01:35] Liam Chen: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our infra; we can provide host affinity notes for contracts. Private deployments give you VPC-only control and can be on-prem if needed.
[01:46] Jordan: Moving to the SIG sheet — we prepared a CSV export of control mappings. I'll share the link in the chat after the call.
[01:54] Alex: Great. On SOC 2 — do you have a Type II and scope? We have a checklist specifically looking for ingestion, storage, and model serving controls.
[02:05] Priya Nair: We have SOC 2 Type II covering the hosted API control set — includes logical access, change management, incident response. I'll attach the report; redactions are standard for third-party vendors. The scope excludes customers' VPCs for private deployments.
[02:20] Alex: And ISO?
[02:23] Jordan: We have ISO 27001 certificate; I'll include cert copy. For ISO evidence, we often provide our ISMS policies and our auditor's letter.
[02:31] Martin: On the VRQ there's a question about third-party crypto modules — FIPS or HSM? We use KMS — how is that managed?
[02:41] Liam Chen: Good question. By default, Redwood-managed KMS (cloud provider KMS) is used; for customers that require it we support BYOK and HSM integrations (you can bring your key material via CMKs). We'll send the architecture options.
[02:53] Priya Patel: Does BYOK require private deployment? Or can it be done on hosted?
[03:00] Liam Chen: BYOK can be enabled on hosted in many cases via customer KMS linked to our service accounts; there are key policies and limited surface area for export. For maximum assurance we recommend Private where KMS is in your VPC.
[03:14] Jordan: We'll note that in the control mapping.
[03:18] [00:03:20] (background noise)
[03:25] Alex: Audit logs — how granular? We need user-level tokens, admin actions, model changes, prompt submission logs? Also retention periods — our policy is 7 years for critical logs.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Redwood stores audit logs with event types: auth events, API calls (including token ID and request metadata), admin console changes, model deployment events. We can provide export in JSON/CSV and configure retention; default is 90 days on hosted, dedicated offers configurable retention, private is under customer control.
[03:52] Sandeep: 90 days won't meet 7-year policy. For longer retention do you offer cold storage exports?
[03:58] Liam Chen: Yes — we can provide periodic exports to S3 (or your archive) and support log shipping to Splunk/Datadog. For compliance we typically provide an evidence bundle and a log export process.
[04:10] Priya Patel: Will the export include request payloads? We have PII constraints.
[04:15] Priya Nair: By default payloads are truncated/anonymized; we have redaction controls. If you need full payload retention that's doable under a contract with data handling agreements and encryption controls. We'll flag that as a custom requirement.
[04:30] Alex: Good. Next, SSO and RBAC — we saw questions about SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, and role hierarchy.
[04:38] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and Role-Based Access Control with admin/owner/editor/viewer; we also support custom roles for Dedicated/Private. Priya, should I hand over to you for specifics?
[04:50] Priya Nair: Yes — we have default roles and an audit trail for role changes. On SAML, we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, metadata exchange, and attribute mapping. SCIM provisioning supports groups and deprovisioning. Some forms ask for screenshots, so we'll provide console screenshots of the SSO configuration screen.
[05:06] Martin: We also need MFA for privileged console logins. Is that enforced?
[05:10] Priya Nair: We enforce MFA for Redwood admin accounts; customers can require MFA via their IdP for SSO flows. We can also enable conditional access policies on Dedicated.
[05:20] Alex: On encryption — at rest and in transit. TLS and what ciphers, and support for customer-controlled keys?
[05:27] Liam Chen: All in-transit is TLS1.2+ (we support 1.3) with strong ciphers. At rest, AES-256 encryption is applied. Customer keys via KMS are supported; we'll include the KMS key policy examples and the HSM options.
[05:40] [00:05:45] (murmur)
[05:47] Priya Patel: The VRQ also has items about vulnerability management — CVE patch cadence and penetration tests.
[05:53] Priya Nair: Redwood runs internal pentests quarterly and engages external pen testers annually. Patch cadence depends on severity; critical patches are hotpatched within our SLA windows and we have a CVE monitoring feed. We'll provide the high-level VM policy and recent pentest summary.
[06:11] Sandeep: For private deployments, do you provide the automation code (IaC) so we can self-audit?
[06:18] Liam Chen: We provide deployment templates and some IaC artifacts; for on-prem we can provide a subset of scripts and an attestation. Full source code is not provided, but we can provide config manifests and installation checklists.
[06:30] Alex: There's a question about personnel background checks and least privilege — can you confirm SOC/HR controls?
[06:37] Jordan: Our HR policy includes background checks for operations and engineering roles; access is role-justified and reviewed. We'll point you to the HR controls section in the SOC 2.
[06:47] Priya Patel: On data residency — the VRQ asks about EU data residency and ability to restrict processing to particular regions.
[06:55] Priya Nair: We support region routing; hosted customers can select region endpoints; Dedicated provides region-specific capacity. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to a region. We'll include region list and data flow diagram.
[07:09] Martin: If we choose hosted but route to EU, does any metadata leave region for analytics?
[07:15] Liam Chen: By default analytics are aggregated; we can configure analytics aggregation to respect region boundaries in enterprise tiers. We'll document that.
[07:24] Jordan: OK — shifting to evidence packaging — you asked for artifacts mapped to each VRQ question. We use a SIG-style mapping where each control maps to a control ID and an evidence link.
[07:36] Alex: Does Redwood provide a machine-readable SIG export or only a PDF?
[07:41] Priya Nair: We can provide both. The machine-readable CSV export has control IDs, yes/no, supplement notes, and links to artifacts (PDFs/screenshots). We'll attach that file.
[07:53] [00:07:55] (keyboard typing)
[07:58] Alex: About evidence redaction — sometimes SOC reports have vendor names or internal IPs redacted; will that be acceptable? Our VRQ expects some raw logs as evidence.
[08:07] Priya Nair: Redactions are normal for third-party SOC docs. For raw logs, we can provide exports under an NDA and data handling agreement; those will be redacted for PII unless agreed otherwise.
[08:20] Martin: Procurement needs assurance that signs of control exceptions are documented. How do you show remediation timelines?
[08:28] Jordan: In our incident response and change management artifacts we include SLAs and post-incident reports. For each exception we provide remediation trackers and timelines; we'll surface a sample.
[08:39] Alex: One of our controls requires WAF and DDoS mitigations — are those in place?
[08:45] Liam Chen: Yes — WAF and DDoS protections at the edge via provider services; for Dedicated we have additional rulesets and can share our config templates.
[08:56] [00:09:00] (brief silence)
[09:02] Priya Patel: Can you show how respond-to-access-requests work? GDPR DSARs — time to respond?
[09:09] Priya Nair: We honor DSARs per our data processing agreement. We have runbooks for subject access requests; typical turnaround depends on scope but internal SLA is 30 days, can be accelerated with contract terms.
[09:21] Sandeep: For GDPR, do you support data deletion in logs and model cache?
[09:27] Liam Chen: We have deletion APIs and retention controls; KV cache eviction policies can be enforced. For hosted customers, deletion can be coordinated via API and we can provide attestations of deletion.
[09:40] Jordan: Are there any high-priority gaps you want us to call out now?
[09:44] Alex: Two things — we need evidence that payloads are not used for model training and a statement on whether inference prompts are persisted beyond short-term caches.
[09:52] Priya Nair: By default Redwood does not use customer prompts to train public models; we have a data usage policy. Persistence is transient in the KV cache for latency (configurable); longer-term retention requires explicit settings. We'll provide the data usage policy and cache behavior doc.
[10:08] Martin: Also need assurance for service continuity — RTO/RPO?
[10:13] Liam Chen: For hosted we publish latency/availability SLOs; RTO/RPO targets are part of Dedicated SLAs. We can share the availability SLA and disaster recovery runbook.
[10:25] [00:10:30] (paper rustle)
[10:32] Alex: On the VRQ, there's an item for supply chain — who are your major subprocessors?
[10:38] Jordan: We maintain a subprocessors list; major ones include cloud providers (names redacted here on call) and certain monitoring vendors. We'll share the subprocessors list and include security attestations for each.
[10:49] Priya Patel: Any automated configuration drift detection?
[10:53] Liam Chen: Yes — we have drift detection and alerting in our infra pipelines and configuration management. We'll include a sample alert and remediation ticket.
[11:05] Alex: For compliance, procurement often wants contract clauses — indemnity limits, breach notification times. Can you share sample contract language?
[11:14] Jordan: We can provide a standard contract redline and sample security addendum. Specific terms are negotiable in enterprise contracts.
[11:22] Martin: Would Redwood consider a site visit or onsite audit for critical vendors?
[11:27] Priya Nair: We accommodate auditor access under NDA for major customers; onsite audits require deeper engagement but can be scheduled. We'll outline the auditor access process.
[11:36] [00:11:40] (crosstalk)
[11:40] Sandeep: For system-level monitoring — metrics retention and access to metrics endpoints?
[11:45] Liam Chen: We expose metrics to customers via the console and have APIs for metric pulls; retention defaults vary, but we can set longer retention for Dedicated and Private.
[11:55] Alex: Can you confirm the identity of the reviewer of the SOC report? Some VRQs request auditor contact.
[12:01] Priya Nair: We cannot disclose auditors' personal contacts on the call, but we'll provide auditor firm name and report references.
[12:10] Jordan: Quick pause — I'm dropping the SIG CSV export and a link to our security pack in chat: https://redwood.ai/security/sig-export-zenith-2025-02-14.csv and https://redwood.ai/security/pack/small-sample.zip (placeholders)
[12:24] Martin: Got it.
[12:28] Alex: About encryption key rotation — what's the cadence and can we audit key rotation events?
[12:33] Liam Chen: Key rotation can be automatic or customer-triggered; rotation events are logged and tied to audit logs. We'll show sample KMS audit entries.
[12:42] Priya Patel: For the VRQ there's an ask for MFA exceptions log — can you produce a list of exceptions or emergency access?
[12:50] Priya Nair: We log emergency access sessions and privileged elevation; privileged access requires justification and is timebound. We can produce an exceptions report under agreement.
[13:02] [00:13:05] (short pause)
[13:08] Alex: Any red flags from your side about what Zenith should expect when mapping the VRQ?
[13:13] Jordan: No immediate red flags; most items are standard and we have mapped controls. Custom requirements like 7-year log retention or full payload archival will need contractual changes or Dedicated/Private deployment.
[13:26] Alex: Noted. For evidence delivery, what's the process — secure link or portal?
[13:33] Jordan: We use secure links for artifacts; for bulk raw logs we use S3 presigned URLs with time-limited access, or we can set up a temporary read-only bucket if needed. All transfers use TLS and signed URLs.
[13:45] Martin: Procurement asks about insurance — cyber liability coverage?
[13:50] Jordan: We carry cyber liability insurance; we'll share the certificate and coverage summary.
[13:57] Priya Patel: A number of VRQ questions require screenshots of architecture diagrams and config screens. Will you do that?
[14:03] Priya Nair: Yes — we'll provide annotated screenshots and architecture diagrams in the evidence pack.
[14:10] Sandeep: For the private deployment, what parts of telemetry still call home to Redwood? We need to know any central control plane interactions.
[14:18] Liam Chen: Private deployments can be configured with a customer-managed control plane; by default the control plane reports usage metrics to Redwood for support, but that can be disabled under customer-hosted control-plane configuration. We'll document control-plane telemetry options.
[14:32] [00:14:35] (breathing)
[14:37] Alex: Let's talk timing — our vendor review window is end of February. If you can get the SIG export and SOC doc by 2/18 that gives us time to review.
[14:47] Jordan: Sounds doable — Jordan to deliver SIG export + control mapping by 2/18. Priya will deliver the audit log demo by 2/20. Liam will deliver KMS runbook by 2/21.
[14:58] Martin: Can we get a written statement on training data usage? It's high priority.
[15:03] Priya Nair: We'll provide the data usage policy and a statement that customer prompts are not used for model training unless contractually agreed.
[15:10] Alex: Great. Anything else?
[15:13] Priya Patel: One last ask — can you provide a sample redacted raw log so we can validate schema?
[15:18] Liam Chen: Yes — we'll include a sample redacted log file with schema description.
[15:23] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the technical deep-dive for KMS and network segmentation — propose 60 minutes next week.
[15:34] Alex: Thanks.
[15:36] [00:15:38] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words, some acronyms spelled phonetically; speaker IDs are mostly accurate but Fireflies auto-attribution sometimes merges two participants.

Referenced artifacts (shared in chat): https://redwood.ai/security/sig-export-zenith-2025-02-14.csv (SIG CSV export), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-type2-2024-redacted.pdf (SOC 2 Type II redacted), https://redwood.ai/security/iso27001-cert.pdf (ISO27001 cert), https://redwood.ai/security/kms-runbook-draft.pdf (KMS options), sample-log-redacted.json (S3 presigned link to be provided).
